name: Crucible ArcShield Welding Gauntlet
description:
Heavy-duty split-leather shell with aluminized dorsal panels and a dense aramid lining, built for sustained arc flash and slag exposure. Stitching is triple-locked with heat-resistant thread; the cuff extends mid-forearm and fastens with a single reinforced snap. Color is a mottled ochre-brown with scorch marks that accumulate as a badge of use.

The right gauntlet ships with a chrome-arm cuff adapter ring, allowing wearers with augmented forearms to snap the gauntlet directly onto a prosthetic wrist collar. The left features a pull-tab quick-release for emergencies.
functionality: Rated to 1,200°C radiant flash. Aug-compatible cuff adapter accommodates standard prosthetic wrist collars. Quick-release left cuff allows single-hand doffing. Reinforced palm patch resists puncture from metal burrs and slag splash.
what_it_says: This person works the real fire — no simulators, no delegating.
story_hooks: A pair found in a the Gray Zone squat still has the previous owner's name stamped inside — and she's on a missing persons board.
The chrome-arm adapter ring is a known fit for a banned military prosthetic model, raising questions about where Crucible's specs came from.
A welder uses the gauntlets to smuggle data chips in the cuff cavity — the aluminized layer masks scanner reads.

physical_description.visual_profile: Heavy industrial welding gauntlet with pronounced protective architecture. Thick, visibly reinforced construction dominates the hand and forearm. The mottled ochre-brown leather reads as battle-worn and functional. Asymmetrical design—right cuff has a chrome adapter ring for augmented limbs, left has an emergency pull-tab. Suggests serious fabrication work, not fashion.
physical_description.fit: Compression fit through the palm and fingers; loose but structured cuff that extends mid-forearm. Designed to accommodate both baseline and augmented wrists. Stiff when new, breaks in with character.
physical_description.primary_material: Split leather shell (ochre-brown) with aluminized dorsal panels (silvered metal strips across back of hand and forearm). Dense aramid lining underneath for arc flash protection.
physical_description.texture: Rough, tooled leather exterior with visible scorch marks and burn patterns. Aluminized panels are smooth and reflective. Triple-locked stitching is thick and prominent. Heat-resistant thread leaves slight texture variation.
physical_description.color_scheme: Mottled ochre-brown base with darker scorch marks and charring accumulating across the leather. Chrome/silver aluminized dorsal panels provide high-contrast accents. Natural patina of industrial use.
physical_description.closures: Single reinforced magnetic snap at the cuff. Left gauntlet features a bright pull-tab quick-release mechanism (likely neon or contrasting material). Right gauntlet has a chrome snap-ring adapter for augmented forearm coupling.
distinctive_features: Aluminized dorsal panels for arc flash deflection
Chrome adapter ring on right cuff for prosthetic wrist coupling
Accumulated scorch marks and burn patterns as working patina
Mid-forearm cuff extension for slag protection
Asymmetrical design—tailored for mixed augmentation scenarios
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 working class. Professional-grade equipment, not luxury, but quality enough to command respect in fabrication zones. The chrome augmentation adapter suggests accessibility to mid-tier corpo or independent fab-shop culture.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer is a fabricator, welder, or industrial technician—likely augmented or working in high-heat environments. Practical, no pretense. The accumulated scorch marks are a badge of competence. Suggests someone who works with their hands and trusts their tools.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and weathered. Scorch marks are expected and accumulated over months or years of use. Leather develops a dark patina. Stitching remains tight and functional. Gauntlets are typically worn as a matched pair despite asymmetrical design.
